proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a law \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and condition on \((M,\Omega)\).  Define
\[
 X_{ju}=\frac{w_{ju}\epsilon_{ju}}s,
 \qquad (j,u)\in I\times J.
\]
The weights are fixed under this conditioning.  Conditional centering gives \(\mathbb E(X_{ju}\mid M,\Omega)=0\).  Conditional row independence and conditional within-row block dependence imply that \(\{X_{ju}\}\), indexed by the subset \(I\times J\subset\mathbb Z_+^2\), is a \(q\)-dependent random field for the maximum metric: two index sets separated by more than \(q\) either lie in distinct rows, or their same-row time coordinates are separated by more than \(q\).

The conditional variance of the sum is exactly one.  Indeed, conditional centering and block dependence make covariances vanish outside lags \(|h|\le q\), common stationary covariance supplies the remaining covariances, and the definition of \(s^2\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_{j,u}X_{ju}\middle|M,\Omega\right)
 &=\frac1{s^2}\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{h=-q}^q\gamma(h)
      \sum_{u=1}^T w_{ju}w_{j,u+h}\\
 &=1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The conditional exponential-moment assumption implies a uniform conditional third-moment bound.  Specifically, the elementary inequality \(|x|^3\le C K^3\exp(x^2/K^2)\) gives
\[
 \sup_{j,u}\mathbb E(|\epsilon_{ju}|^3\mid M,\Omega)\le C K^3
\]
almost surely.  Apply the cited Chen--Shao finite-range random-field bound with \(p_0=3\), \(d_0=2\), and \(k_0=q\).  Conditional on \((M,\Omega)\), it yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P\!\left(\frac Ls\le z\middle|M,\Omega\right)-\Phi(z)\right|
 &\le 75(10q+1)^4\sum_{j,u}\mathbb E(|X_{ju}|^3\mid M,\Omega)\\
 &\le C_qK^3
   \frac{\max_{j,u}|w_{ju}|}{s}
   \frac{\sum_{j,u}w_{ju}^2}{s^2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first normalized weight factor is \(o(1)\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), and the second is \(O(1)\) uniformly, by the established score-diffuseness lemma.  The displayed conditional Kolmogorov distance therefore tends to zero uniformly over the class, which is the asserted conditional central limit theorem.

Let \(q=0\), \(H=1\), and \(W=\{t_0\}\).  Average the complete tangent identity over \(i\in G\).  With \(\bar x_G=g^{-1}\sum_{i\in G}x_i\), \(A=A_{t_0}\), and \(B=B_S\), this gives the exact decomposition
\[
 L=\mathcal D_n+\mathcal T_n-\mathcal O_n,
\]
where
\[
 \mathcal D_n=\sum_{j\in C(t_0)}\bar x_G^\top A^{-1}x_j\epsilon_{j,t_0},
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_n=\frac1g\sum_{i\in G}\sum_{u\in S}
 f_{t_0}^\top B^{-1}f_u\epsilon_{iu},
\]
and \(\mathcal O_n\) is the donor--pretreatment overlap score defined in the one-date curvature lemma.  That lemma proves both
\[
 \mathcal O_n=o_{\mathbb P}(s),
 \qquad B_2=o_{\mathbb P}(s).
\]

When \(q=0\), the coordinates entering \(\mathcal D_n\), \(\mathcal T_n\), and \(\mathcal O_n\) are pairwise disjoint and conditionally independent.  Therefore the variance of the two-term leading score is
\[
 V_{\mathrm{CY}}
 =\operatorname{Var}(\mathcal D_n+\mathcal T_n\mid M,\Omega)
 =\gamma(0)\left\{
   \bar x_G^\top A^{-1}\bar x_G
   +\frac1g f_{t_0}^\top B^{-1}f_{t_0}
 \right\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 s^2=V_{\mathrm{CY}}+\operatorname{Var}(\mathcal O_n\mid M,\Omega),
 \qquad
 \frac{\operatorname{Var}(\mathcal O_n\mid M,\Omega)}{s^2}=o(1),
\]
so \(V_{\mathrm{CY}}/s^2\to1\).

The variance is invariant to the scaling used for the singular factors.  Indeed, because \(x_j=D^{1/2}U_{j\cdot}^\top\) and \(f_u=D^{1/2}V_{u\cdot}^\top\),
\[
 \bar x_G^\top A^{-1}\bar x_G
 =\bar U_G^\top
   \left(\sum_{j\in C(t_0)}U_{j\cdot}^\top U_{j\cdot}\right)^{-1}
   \bar U_G,
\]
and
\[
 f_{t_0}^\top B^{-1}f_{t_0}
 =V_{t_0\cdot}
   \left(\sum_{u\in S}V_{u\cdot}^\top V_{u\cdot}\right)^{-1}
   V_{t_0\cdot}^\top.
\]
These are exactly the donor-loading and group-size-scaled pretreatment-factor quadratic forms displayed in Choi and Yuan (2024), Theorem 3.1.  The cited theorem supplies the published one-date group central limit theorem under its stated conditions.  The identities above show that the first two components of the complete score and their variance are its leading score and variance, while the established \(o_{\mathbb P}(s)\) bound shows that the donor--pretreatment overlap is absorbed at that scale.  Together with \(B_2=o_{\mathbb P}(s)\), this proves the claimed reduction.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(d_0,k_0\in\mathbb N\), let \(2<p_0\le 3\), and let \(\mathcal J_0\) be a finite subset of \(\mathbb Z_+^{d_0}\).  Suppose that \(\{X_u:u\in\mathcal J_0\}\) is a centered \(k_0\)-dependent random field, \(\mathbb E|X_u|^{p_0}<\infty\), \(W_0=\sum_{u\in\mathcal J_0}X_u\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(W_0)=1\).  If \(F_0\) is the distribution function of \(W_0\), then
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|F_0(z)-\Phi(z)|
 \le 75(10k_0+1)^{(p_0-1)d_0}
       \sum_{u\in\mathcal J_0}\mathbb E|X_u|^{p_0}.
\]

attestation.note: The hypotheses, normalization, and uniform bound were checked directly against Theorem 2.6 and equation (2.11) in the arXiv source on 2026-09-14.

added_lemmas.justification: This finite-range Berry--Esseen inequality converts the primitive dependence and third-moment bounds into the required conditional Gaussian approximation.
added_lemmas.gap: It is classical probability substrate; the application to the complete causal-panel influence array is proved separately in this note.
added_lemmas.consumer: The uniform score central limit lemma invokes the bound conditionally on the signal and deterministic mask.

added_lemmas.statement: Under conditions (i)--(v) of Choi and Yuan (2024), Theorem 3.1, their common-adoption, one-date subgroup matrix-completion estimator has a group-average imputation error which, after division by the square root of their displayed variance, converges in distribution to a standard normal variable.  Their variance is the sum of a donor-loading quadratic form and a group-size-scaled pretreatment-factor quadratic form.

added_lemmas.consumer: The published-reduction proposition uses the theorem only after proving the factor-scaling and negligible-term map.

added_lemmas.statement:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), specialize to \(q=0\) and \(H=1\), and write \(W=\{t_0\}\).  Define the aggregate donor--pretreatment overlap score
\[
 \mathcal O_n
 =\frac1g\sum_{i\in G}\sum_{j\in C(t_0)}\sum_{u\in S}
   a_{ij,t_0}b_{t_0,u}\epsilon_{ju}.
\]
Then \(\mathcal O_n=o_{\mathbb P}(s)\) and \(B_2=o_{\mathbb P}(s)\).  In fact,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\mathcal O_n\mid M,\Omega)=O(n^{-2}),
 \qquad |B_2|=O(\psi^{-1}),
\]
where both bounds are uniform with constants depending only on the fixed class constants.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), put \(t_0\) for the unique member of \(W\), and condition throughout on \((M,\Omega)\).  The conditional exponential-moment assumption and Jensen's inequality give
\[
 \exp\!\left\{\frac{\mathbb E(\epsilon_{ju}^2\mid M)}{K^2}\right\}
 \le \mathbb E\!\left[\exp\!\left(\frac{\epsilon_{ju}^2}{K^2}\right)\middle|M\right]
 \le 2.
\]
Thus \(\gamma(0)\le K^2\log 2\).  When \(q=0\), conditional row independence and conditional block dependence imply conditional independence of all distinct noise coordinates.

We first record the leverage and coefficient bounds used below.  Write \(x_i^\top\) and \(f_u^\top\) for the rows of \(X\) and \(F\), and abbreviate \(A=A_{t_0}\) and \(B=B_S\).  The normalized restricted-Gram assumptions imply
\[
 A^{-1}\preceq c_A^{-1}D^{-1},
 \qquad B^{-1}\preceq c_B^{-1}D^{-1}.
\]
Moreover, incoherence and balanced growth give, uniformly in \(i\) and \(u\),
\[
 x_i^\top D^{-1}x_i=\|U_{i\cdot}\|_2^2\le \frac{\mu r}{N}=O(n^{-1}),
 \qquad
 f_u^\top D^{-1}f_u=\|V_{u\cdot}\|_2^2\le \frac{\mu r}{T}=O(n^{-1}).
\]
Consequently, if
\[
 c_i=x_i^\top A^{-1}x_i,
 \qquad d_0=f_{t_0}^\top B^{-1}f_{t_0},
\]
then \(c_i=O(n^{-1})\) and \(d_0=O(n^{-1})\).  Directly from the definitions of the tangent weights,
\[
 \sum_{j\in C(t_0)}a_{ij,t_0}^2=c_i,
 \qquad
 \sum_{u\in S}b_{t_0,u}^2=d_0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j\in C(t_0),u\in S}a_{ij,t_0}^2b_{t_0,u}^2=c_id_0.
\]
The three coordinate sets in the complete tangent score are disjoint.  Hence the squared Euclidean norm of its observed-coordinate coefficient vector is \(c_i+d_0+c_id_0=O(n^{-1})\).

For the aggregate overlap, set \(\bar x_G=g^{-1}\sum_{i\in G}x_i\) and \(\bar a_j=\bar x_G^\top A^{-1}x_j\).  Convexity of the squared norm and incoherence show
\[
 \bar x_G^\top D^{-1}\bar x_G
 \le \frac1g\sum_{i\in G}x_i^\top D^{-1}x_i=O(n^{-1}).
\]
It follows that
\[
 \sum_{j\in C(t_0)}\bar a_j^2
 =\bar x_G^\top A^{-1}\bar x_G=O(n^{-1}).
\]
Conditional independence of distinct coordinates now yields
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\mathcal O_n\mid M,\Omega)
 =\gamma(0)
   \left(\sum_{j\in C(t_0)}\bar a_j^2\right)
   \left(\sum_{u\in S}b_{t_0,u}^2\right)
 =O(n^{-2}).
\]
Since variance nondegeneracy with \(H=1\) gives \(s^2\ge c_s/n\), conditional Chebyshev's inequality proves \(\mathcal O_n=o_{\mathbb P}(s)\), uniformly over the class.

It remains to control the curvature mean.  Consider one local signal, and let
\(
 M^{it_0}=\mathsf U\mathsf D\mathsf V^\top
\)
be a compact singular value decomposition, with orthogonal complements \(\mathsf U_\perp\) and \(\mathsf V_\perp\).  For a perturbation \(Z\), introduce the blocks
\[
 \mathsf B=\mathsf U^\top Z\mathsf V_\perp,
 \qquad
 \mathsf C=\mathsf U_\perp^\top Z\mathsf V,
 \qquad
 \mathsf D_0=\mathsf U_\perp^\top Z\mathsf V_\perp.
\]
The quadratic coefficient of the best rank-\(r\) projection is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_{it_0}(Z)
 ={}&\mathsf U_\perp\mathsf D_0\mathsf B^\top\mathsf D^{-1}\mathsf V^\top
 +\mathsf U\mathsf D^{-1}\mathsf C^\top\mathsf D_0\mathsf V_\perp^\top\\
 &+\mathsf U_\perp\mathsf C\mathsf D^{-1}\mathsf B\mathsf V_\perp^\top.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For completeness, this identity follows by writing every nearby rank-\(r\) matrix, in the displayed orthogonal coordinates, as
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}
  \mathsf D+R&S\\ T&T(\mathsf D+R)^{-1}S
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Expanding the Frobenius normal equations for projection of
\(
 \left(\begin{smallmatrix}\mathsf D&0\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)
 +\zeta\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\mathsf A&\mathsf B\\\mathsf C&\mathsf D_0\end{smallmatrix}\right)
\)
gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R&=\zeta\mathsf A+O(\zeta^3),\\
 S&=\zeta\mathsf B+\zeta^2\mathsf D^{-1}\mathsf C^\top\mathsf D_0+O(\zeta^3),\\
 T&=\zeta\mathsf C+\zeta^2\mathsf D_0\mathsf B^\top\mathsf D^{-1}+O(\zeta^3),\\
 T(\mathsf D+R)^{-1}S&=\zeta^2\mathsf C\mathsf D^{-1}\mathsf B+O(\zeta^3),
 \end{aligned}
\]
which proves the formula because \(Q_{it_0}=\tfrac12D^2\mathcal P_r(M^{it_0})\).  Only \(\sigma_r(M^{it_0})>0\) is used; repeated positive singular values cause no difficulty in this coordinate chart.  The formula also implies
\[
 \bigl|[Q_{it_0}(Z)]_{it_0}\bigr|
 \le \frac{3}{\sigma_r(M^{it_0})}\|Z\|_F^2.
\]

Let \(e_k\) denote the vectorized target coordinate and let \(l_{it_0}\) be the observed-coordinate coefficient vector of \(\ell_{it_0}\), extended by zero at the target.  For observed noise \(E=P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it_0}}R_{it_0}\epsilon\), the first-order completed perturbation is
\(
 Z_1=E+\ell_{it_0}(E)E^{it_0}_{it_0}
\), and the preceding coefficient calculation gives \(\|l_{it_0}\|_2^2=O(n^{-1})\).  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\operatorname{vec}Z_1\mid M,\Omega)
 =\gamma(0)(I+\mathsf R_{it_0}),
\]
where
\[
 \mathsf R_{it_0}
 =-e_ke_k^\top+e_kl_{it_0}^\top+l_{it_0}e_k^\top
   +\|l_{it_0}\|_2^2e_ke_k^\top.
\]
This matrix has rank at most two and uniformly bounded operator norm.  For a perturbation having identity covariance, each of the three displayed terms in \(Q_{it_0}\) has mean zero: the first uses \(\mathsf U_\perp^\top\mathsf U=0\), the second uses \(\mathsf V_\perp^\top\mathsf V=0\), and the third uses both orthogonalities.  Representing the scalar quadratic form \(Z\mapsto[Q_{it_0}(Z)]_{it_0}\) by a symmetric matrix \(\mathsf H_{it_0}\), the preceding norm bound gives
\(
 \|\mathsf H_{it_0}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 3/\sigma_r(M^{it_0})
\).  Hence
\[
 \left|\mathbb E\{[Q_{it_0}(Z_1)]_{it_0}\mid M,\Omega\}\right|
 =\gamma(0)|\operatorname{tr}(\mathsf H_{it_0}\mathsf R_{it_0})|
 \le \frac{C\gamma(0)}{\sigma_r(M^{it_0})}.
\]

Finally, the row and column leverages of the local signal at the target are, by the Sherman--Morrison formula,
\[
 \pi_i=\frac{c_i}{1+c_i},
 \qquad \nu_{t_0}=\frac{d_0}{1+d_0}.
\]
Thus \(h_{it_0}=\pi_i+\nu_{t_0}-\pi_i\nu_{t_0}=O(n^{-1})\), so \((1-h_{it_0})^{-1}\le2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  By the definition of \(q_{it_0}\), the local-signal lower bound, and the preceding trace estimate,
\[
 |B_2|
 \le \frac1g\sum_{i\in G}
       \frac{C\gamma(0)}{(1-h_{it_0})\sigma_r(M^{it_0})}
 \le \frac{C}{\psi}.
\]
Since \(s\ge\sqrt{c_s/n}\) and the signal envelope at \(H=1\) gives
\(
 \psi\ge n^{1/2+\eta}\ell_n^8
\),
\[
 \frac{|B_2|}{s}\le C\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi}
 \le Cn^{-\eta}\ell_n^{-8}\longrightarrow0.
\]
This proves both assertions uniformly.

added_lemmas.gap: The published theorem suppresses these terms at its scale but does not state the complete three-term differential or this Hessian trace calculation.

proposed.citation: Chen, L. H. Y., and Q.-M. Shao (2004). Normal approximation under local dependence. Annals of Probability 32(3A), 1985--2028. arXiv:math/0410104. DOI: 10.1214/009117904000000450.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof invokes Theorem 2.6, so the primary-source bibliographic record must be present in the core.

proposed.statement:
Conditional on \((M,\Omega)\), fixed \(q\), uniform conditional sub-Gaussian moments, row-law factorization, conditional within-row block dependence, variance nondegeneracy, and the derived score-diffuseness bounds imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P(L/s\le z\mid M,\Omega)-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
proposed.justification: A uniform finite-range random-field Berry--Esseen argument derives the Gaussian limit from primitive conditional dependence, moments, and diffuse weights.
proposed.gap: Existing serial factor central limit theorems do not cover this complete three-block influence array under deterministic causal-block masking.
proposed.consumer: The Wald theorem uses this derived score limit instead of assuming asymptotic normality.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The conditional proof uses the snapshot's conditional exponential-moment assumption and the cited finite-range normal-approximation theorem; both load-bearing dependencies were absent from the node.

proposed.statement: In the special case \(q=0\) and \(H=1\), with the corresponding one-date Choi--Yuan subgroup conditions, \(B_2=o(s)\), the third overlap score is absorbed at their pointwise scale, and the standardized leading score and variance reduce to the group central limit theorem and variance formula in Choi and Yuan (2024), Theorem 3.1.
proposed.justification: The reduction guards against changing the estimand or estimator while enlarging the dependence and target regimes.
proposed.gap: The published theorem is the reduction target rather than an unresolved result.
proposed.consumer: Applied users recover the existing one-date procedure when no serial or window correction is needed.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The reduction is proved directly from a new curvature-overlap lemma and a source-verified cited leaf; it does not depend on the still-open growing-window Wald theorem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A uniform second-order expansion of the implemented masked nuclear-norm fixed point, including simultaneous active-rank stability, centered aggregation across overlapping local fits, regularization and cubic errors, pretreatment reconstruction, curvature plug-in stability, and relative fitted-weight consistency.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact proximal identity is a nonsmooth self-consistency equation. The frozen assumptions and established lemmas do not provide a uniform contraction or active-rank neighborhood for every native fit, nor a concentration theorem for the aggregate of their shared-data quadratic and higher-order terms. Pointwise projector Taylor formulas and nonexpansiveness do not imply the asserted signed aggregate rates.
open_obligations.attempted: The optimizer was reduced to its exact singular-value-thresholding fixed point, the complete differential and target-coordinate auxiliary separation were retained, and every asserted raw error was converted to the oracle standard-error scale. The prescribed interior exponent check closes conditionally on those raw rates, but deriving the rates from the native optimizer remains the missing new argument.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The established proximal identity, complete tangent formula, and auxiliary measurability result reduce the unresolved part to one precise native-map estimate.  The actual optimizer satisfies
\[
 \widetilde M^{it}=\operatorname{SVT}_{\lambda}\!\left(
 P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
 +P_{(\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it})^c}\widetilde M^{it}
 \right),
\]
and the first differential of the associated completion branch is the declared donor-window plus treated-pre minus donor-pre score.  The neighborhood-replaced fit is conditionally separated from the target coordinate.  These facts do not supply a uniform differentiable branch for the nonsmooth self-consistent map.

If the raw bounds in the target theorem are established, their standard-error consequences are deterministic.  From \(s\ge c(nH)^{-1/2}\) and \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac{|Q-B_2|}{s}
 &=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt H}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}\right),\\
 \frac{|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|}{s}
 &=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
   \frac{\ell_n^4n\sqrt H}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}
   +\frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt H}{n}
 \right),\\
 \frac{|\widehat B_2-B_2|}{s}
 &=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
   \frac{\ell_n^4n\sqrt H}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}
   +\frac{\Delta_\gamma\sqrt{nH}}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}
 \right).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Under the stated signal envelope, the first three deterministic factors are bounded by constant multiples of
\[
 n^{-1/2-\eta}H^{1/4}\ell_n^{-4},
 \qquad n^{-2\eta}\ell_n^{-12},
 \qquad \ell_n^4\sqrt H/n,
\]
which vanish because \(H\le Cn\).  The asserted pretreatment rate and \(m\asymp n\) would also give \(\Delta_\gamma=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2n^{-1/2})\), making the covariance plug-in ratio vanish.

For the prescribed interior calibration \(H\asymp n\) and \(\psi=n^{4/5}\), the asserted raw rates would imply
\[
 n|Q-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4n^{-3/10}),
 \qquad
 n|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4n^{-1/10}+\ell_n^4n^{-1/2}),
\]
and
\[
 n|\widehat B_2-B_2|
 =O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4n^{-1/10}+\ell_n^2n^{-3/10}),
\]
so all three would vanish.  This verifies the exponent arithmetic but does not certify the implemented optimizer: the missing statement remains the uniform native fixed-point expansion and its centered aggregate concentration.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The native expansion, feasible curvature rate, and relative fitted-weight rate needed before the proved score limit can be studentized.
open_obligations.obstruction: The causal cancellation, variance comparison, and conditional Gaussian limit are now closed, but the theorem still depends on the unresolved native second-order transfer target. Claiming coverage without that estimator-specific bridge would treat its hard conclusion as an assumption.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact causal error identity and banded-Toeplitz variance bound were combined with the now-proved conditional score central limit theorem. This reduces every remaining term to a conclusion stated, but not yet proved, in the native-transfer theorem.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The conditional score central limit theorem is proved in this dispatch.  The causal and studentization reductions are exact.  Consistency and the common-start mask give \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}=Y_{it}(1)\) on \(G\times W\), hence
\[
 \widehat\tau-\tau
 =-\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it}).
\]
If the native second-order target is established, the definitions of the correction and remainder then give
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau
 =-L-(Q-B_2)-R_{\mathrm{agg}}+(\widehat B_2-B_2)
 =-L+o_{\mathbb P}(s).
\]

For variance estimation, put \(d=\widehat w-w\), and let \(\Gamma_q\) and \(\widehat\Gamma_q\) be the banded Toeplitz matrices generated by \(\gamma\) and \(\widehat\gamma\).  Fixed \(q\), the conditional moment bound, and \(\Delta_\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) give bounded operator norms and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat V-s^2|
 &\le \|\widehat\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
       \left(2\|w\|_F\|d\|_F+\|d\|_F^2\right)
       +\|\widehat\Gamma_q-\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|w\|_F^2\\
 &\le C_q\left\{
   \|w\|_F\|d\|_F+\|d\|_F^2+\Delta_\gamma\|w\|_F^2
 \right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Score diffuseness gives \(\|w\|_F^2=O(s^2)\).  Thus the fitted-weight conclusion of the native target and \(\Delta_\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) imply \(\widehat V/s^2\to_{\mathbb P}1\).  Conditional Slutsky applied to the now-proved score limit then yields the stated studentized limit and Wald coverage.  Therefore the only unclosed premise for this theorem is the native second-order transfer and its plug-in conclusions.

proposed.statement: On the complete rank-one alternating-factor calibration array with \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}=1/2\), let \(p_t=1+\tfrac12(-1)^t\). In the target chart \(I_{it}\times J_{it}\), the exact formula \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/\psi=\sqrt{(3/4+1/n)\{1/2+4p_t^2/(5n)\}}\) implies \(\inf_{i,t}\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/\psi>c_{\mathrm{loc}}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\) and \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/\psi\to\sqrt{3/8}\). Direct contraction of the rank-one projector Hessian against the moving-average covariance in that same chart gives \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}\,\mathbb E[q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)\mid M]\to-6\sqrt{3/2}\,p_t/(5\sqrt5)\), and therefore \(\psi\,\mathbb E[q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)\mid M]\to\kappa^{\mathrm{drift}}_t=-2\gamma(1)p_t(n/m)(1-\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}^2)/(1+\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}^2)^{3/2}=-12p_t/(5\sqrt5)\) for every fixed parity of \(t\in W\). Thus the global-signal limits are \(-18/(5\sqrt5)\) for even targets and \(-6/(5\sqrt5)\) for odd targets, and \(\psi B_2\to-12/(5\sqrt5)\) because the consecutive window contains equally many targets of each parity. For the native masked optimizer with \(\lambda_n=4\sqrt n\log(n+2)\) and \(\psi=n^{4/5}\), the fitted correction removes this drift and \(n\{(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})-L-\widehat B_2\}\to_{\mathbb P}0\).
proposed.justification: The explicit parity constants replace an unsupported universal value and make the early kill test reproducible for the precise mask, factor normalization, dependence law, and penalty used by the native optimizer.
proposed.gap: Neither the independent-noise MNAR theorem nor fully observed leave-neighbor PCA contains this masked rank-projection coefficient.
proposed.consumer: A closed-form calibration case detects omitted interior overlap or regularization terms before empirical use.

obligation.what_is_open: The raw native masked-optimizer expansion and feasible curvature plug-in bounds invoked through the added transfer-theorem dependency.
obligation.obstruction: The calibration algebra reduces the desired panel-scaled conclusion to the stated raw rates, but the sibling transfer theorem is not established. The exact proximal identity alone gives neither the signed averaging gain nor control of regularization and fitted-Hessian errors.
obligation.attempted: Verified the local singular value, the rank-one Hessian contraction, the parity average, all calibration-array member conditions needed for the transfer theorem, and the exact rate substitution. Nonexpansiveness of singular-value thresholding is only a pointwise norm bound and does not yield the required inverse-panel aggregate rate.
obligation.partial_result:
The oracle calibration and the reduction of the last assertion to the sibling transfer theorem are complete.  There are \(3n/4+1\) rows in \(I_{it}\).  Since \(n\in8\mathbb N\), each of \(S\) and \(W\) contains equally many even and odd indices, and
\[
\sum_{s\in S}p_s^2=\frac{5n}{8},
\qquad
\|u^{\mathrm{cal}}_{I_{it}}\|_2^2=\frac34+\frac1n,
\qquad
\|v^{\mathrm{cal}}_{J_{it}}\|_2^2=\frac12+\frac{4p_t^2}{5n}.
\]
The local signal is the rank-one matrix \(\psi u^{\mathrm{cal}}_{I_{it}}(v^{\mathrm{cal}}_{J_{it}})^\top\).  Positivity of both displayed squared norms therefore gives
\[
\frac{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}}{\psi}
=
\sqrt{\left(\frac34+\frac1n\right)
\left(\frac12+\frac{4p_t^2}{5n}\right)}
\longrightarrow\sqrt{\frac38}>\frac12,
\]
uniformly over the two possible values of \(p_t\).

The moving-average definition gives, using independence and unit variance of the innovations,
\[
\gamma(0)=\mathbb E\left[\left(z_{it}+\frac12z_{i,t-1}\right)^2\right]=\frac54,
\qquad
\gamma(1)=\mathbb E\left[\left(z_{it}+\frac12z_{i,t-1}\right)
\left(z_{i,t+1}+\frac12z_{it}\right)\right]=\frac12,
\]
where the second display is read as the expectation of the product of its two parenthesized factors, and \(\gamma(h)=0\) for \(|h|>1\).  Normalize the local signal as \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}uv^\top\), and, for a perturbation \(E\), put
\[
c_E=(I-uu^\top)Ev,\qquad
b_E=(I-vv^\top)E^\top u,\qquad
\mathscr D_E=(I-uu^\top)E(I-vv^\top).
\]
The rank-one singular-subspace equations, expanded through homogeneous degree two, give the quadratic term
\[
Q_{it}(E)
=
\frac{\mathscr D_Eb_Ev^\top+u c_E^\top\mathscr D_E+c_Eb_E^\top}
{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}}.
\]
The already established complete tangent score supplies the donor-window, treated-pre, and negative donor-pre terms.  Substituting
\[
E=P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon+
\ell_{it}(R_{it}\epsilon)E^{it}_{it}
\]
into the preceding homogeneous quadratic map and contracting the only nonzero same-row covariances, at lags zero and one, gives
\[
\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}\,
\mathbb E\!\left[
q_{it}\!\left(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon\right)
\middle|M\right]
=-\frac{6\sqrt{3/2}}{5\sqrt5}\,p_t+O(n^{-1}).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\psi\,
\mathbb E\!\left[
q_{it}\!\left(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon\right)
\middle|M\right]
\longrightarrow-\frac{12p_t}{5\sqrt5}
=\kappa_t^{\mathrm{drift}}.
\]
Thus the limits are \(-18/(5\sqrt5)\) and \(-6/(5\sqrt5)\) for even and odd \(t\), respectively.  Since \(H=n/4\) is even, averaging the two parities proves
\[
\psi B_2\longrightarrow-\frac{12}{5\sqrt5}.
\]

The calibration also satisfies the premises needed to specialize the sibling transfer theorem.  Indeed \(A_t=3\psi/4\), \(B_S=\psi/2\), the local condition number is one, and the incoherence constant can be chosen as \(9/5\).  The Gaussian moving-average rows are independent across rows, centered, uniformly sub-Gaussian, and one-dependent.  For the oracle aggregate score, \(a_{ij,t}=4/(3n)\) and \(b_{t,s}=8p_tp_s/(5n)\).  Hence its nonzero aggregate weights are
\[
w_{is}=\frac{32p_s}{5n^2}\quad(i\in G,\ s\in S),
\qquad
w_{jt}=\frac{16}{3n^2}\quad(j\notin G,\ t\in W),
\qquad
w_{js}=-\frac{32p_s}{15n^2}\quad(j\notin G,\ s\in S).
\]
The moving-average covariance matrix has eigenvalues between \(1/4\) and \(9/4\), because its transfer polynomial is \(1+\tfrac12e^{-{\rm i}\omega}\).  Direct summation gives
\[
\sum_{i,u}w_{iu}^2
=
\left(\frac{32}{5}+\frac{16}{3}+\frac{32}{15}\right)n^{-2}
=\frac{208}{15}n^{-2}.
\]
The preperiod and window are separated by two calendar periods, so their covariance is zero under one-dependence.  It follows that \(s^2\asymp n^{-2}\asymp(nH)^{-1}\), verifying variance nondegeneracy.  Finally, for any fixed \(\eta\in(0,1/20)\),
\[
\frac{\psi}{n^{1/2+\eta}H^{1/4}\ell_n^8}
=4^{1/4}\frac{n^{1/20-\eta}}{\ell_n^8}
\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
and the specified penalty has the required \(\sqrt n\,\ell_n\) order.

It remains only to invoke the presently unproved raw conclusions of \(\mathrm{thm:native\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}transfer}\).  Write
\[
\mathcal R_n=
\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})
-L-\widehat B_2.
\]
Its decomposition gives
\[
\mathcal R_n=(Q-B_2)+R_{\mathrm{agg}}-(\widehat B_2-B_2).
\]
Since \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\psi/2=n^{4/5}/2\), \(m=n/2\), and \(\ell_n=\log(n+2)\), the claimed fit and covariance bounds imply
\[
\Delta_\gamma
=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{m}}+\frac{\log n}{m}
+\frac{\ell_n^2}{\sqrt n}+\frac{\ell_n^4}{n}
\right)
=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\frac{\ell_n^2}{\sqrt n}\right).
\]
Multiplying each raw remainder bound by \(n\) then yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
n|Q-B_2|
&=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4n^{-3/10}),\\
n|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|
&=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\ell_n^4n^{-1/10}
+\ell_n^4n^{-1/2}\right),\\
n|\widehat B_2-B_2|
&=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\ell_n^4n^{-1/10}
+\ell_n^2n^{-3/10}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every displayed deterministic rate tends to zero.  Therefore those raw transfer bounds would imply \(n\mathcal R_n\to_{\mathbb P}0\).  The unresolved step is the proof of those native-optimizer bounds, not the calibration algebra or the rate reduction.

A direct use of proximal nonexpansiveness loses the averaging gain and leaves the penalty and fitted-Hessian terms uncontrolled.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The exact calibration calculation is complete:
\[
\frac{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}}{\psi}
=\sqrt{\left(\frac34+\frac1n\right)
\left(\frac12+\frac{4p_t^2}{5n}\right)}
\longrightarrow\sqrt{\frac38}>\frac12.
\]
The exact rank-one projector expansion and contraction of the lag-zero and lag-one covariances give
\[
\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}\,
\mathbb E\!\left[
q_{it}\!\left(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon\right)
\middle|M\right]
=-\frac{6\sqrt{3/2}}{5\sqrt5}\,p_t+O(n^{-1}),
\]
and hence
\[
\psi\,
\mathbb E\!\left[
q_{it}\!\left(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon\right)
\middle|M\right]
\longrightarrow-\frac{12p_t}{5\sqrt5}.
\]
Because the consecutive window contains equally many even and odd indices,
\[
\psi B_2\longrightarrow-\frac{12}{5\sqrt5}.
\]
The calibration has donor and preperiod normalized Grams \(3/4\) and \(1/2\), local condition number one, incoherence bounded by \(9/5\), independent Gaussian one-dependent rows, and \(s^2\asymp(nH)^{-1}\).  It obeys the signal-window envelope for every fixed \(\eta\in(0,1/20)\).

If the raw conclusions of \(\mathrm{thm:native\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}transfer}\) hold, then with
\[
\mathcal R_n=
\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})
-L-\widehat B_2
\]
and \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge n^{4/5}/2\), their decomposition and triangle inequality give
\[
\begin{aligned}
n|\mathcal R_n|
&\le n|Q-B_2|+n|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|+n|\widehat B_2-B_2|\\
&=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
\ell_n^4n^{-1/10}
+\ell_n^4n^{-3/10}
+\ell_n^4n^{-1/2}
+\ell_n^2n^{-3/10}
\right)
=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the target's final assertion is an exact rate corollary of that sibling theorem.  What remains open is the native-optimizer proof of the raw bounds themselves.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a compact set \(\mathcal K\subset [1/2,1]\times(0,1]\times[0,1]\), and condition throughout on \((M,\Omega)\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:deterministic\mbox{-}mask}\), conditioning on \(\Omega\) adds no randomness after conditioning on \(M\).  The oracle definition gives
\[
 \frac{L}{s}=\sum_{j\in I}\sum_{u\in J}X_{ju},
 \qquad
 X_{ju}:=\frac{w_{ju}\epsilon_{ju}}{s}.
\]
The weights are fixed under the conditional law.  By \(\mathrm{ass:centered\mbox{-}noise}\), \(\mathbb E[X_{ju}\mid M,\Omega]=0\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:independent\mbox{-}rows}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}dependence}\), two vertices \((j,u)\) and \((k,v)\) can be conditionally dependent only if \(j=k\) and \(|u-v|\le q\).  Thus the variables have a dependency graph of maximum degree at most \(2q\), where \(q\) is fixed by \(\mathrm{ass:fixed\mbox{-}known\mbox{-}range}\).

The added member property \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}subgaussian\mbox{-}noise}\) states that, almost surely,
\[
 \sup_{j,u}\mathbb E\!\left[\exp\!\left(\epsilon_{ju}^{2}/K^{2}\right)\middle|M\right]\le 2.
\]
Because \(\Omega\) is deterministic, the same inequality holds conditional on \((M,\Omega)\).  Markov's inequality and the tail integral formula therefore give, for every \(p>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P(|\epsilon_{ju}|>x\mid M,\Omega)
 \le 2e^{-x^{2}/K^{2}},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E(|\epsilon_{ju}|^{p}\mid M,\Omega)
 \le pK^{p}\Gamma(p/2)=:C_pK^p.
\tag{1}
\]
The exact value of \(C_p\) is immaterial and is uniform in the law and the exponent triple.

Set
\[
 A_n:=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(a,b,c),\,(a,b,c)\in\mathcal K}
       \frac{\sum_{j,u}w_{ju}^{2}}{s^{2}},
 \qquad
 \delta_n:=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(a,b,c),\,(a,b,c)\in\mathcal K}
       \frac{\max_{j,u}|w_{ju}|}{s}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:frontier\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}diffuseness}\), \(\sup_n A_n<\infty\) and \(\delta_n\to0\).  Put \(\bar\delta_n=\max\{\delta_n,n^{-1}\}\) and \(k_n=\lfloor\bar\delta_n^{-1}\rfloor\).  Then \(k_n\to\infty\) and \(k_n\delta_n^2\le\bar\delta_n\to0\).

For each row, partition the ordered times into retained consecutive blocks of length at most \(k_n\), separated by gaps of \(q\) deleted times.  The origin of this periodic partition may be chosen separately for each row.  Averaging the squared deleted weights over the \(k_n+q\) possible origins shows that one origin satisfies
\[
 sum_{(j,u)\in D_n}w_{ju}^{2}
 \le \frac{q}{k_n+q}\sum_{j,u}w_{ju}^{2}.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, for a fixed row and a uniform origin, each time index belongs to a gap for at most \(q\) of the \(k_n+q\) origins; summing this incidence identity against \(w_{ju}^{2}\) proves (2), with endpoint indices only reducing the incidence count.  Let
\[
 R_n:=\sum_{(j,u)\in D_n}X_{ju}.
\]
For any deterministic coefficients \(a_{ju}\), conditional centering, the dependency graph, Cauchy--Schwarz, and (1) with \(p=2\) imply
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_{j,u}a_{ju}\epsilon_{ju}\middle|M,\Omega\right)
 \le C_2K^2(2q+1)\sum_{j,u}a_{ju}^{2}.
\tag{3}
\]
Applying (3) to the deleted coefficients and using (2) yields
\[
 \sup_{P,(a,b,c)\in\mathcal K}
 \operatorname{Var}(R_n\mid M,\Omega)
 \le C_qK^2\frac{q}{k_n+q}A_n=o(1).
\tag{4}
\]

Write \(Z_B:=\sum_{(j,u)\in B}X_{ju}\) for a retained block \(B\).  Distinct retained blocks are conditionally independent: different rows are independent, and consecutive retained blocks in one row are separated by \(q\) deleted indices, so their closest indices differ by \(q+1\).  To bound a block's fourth moment, split its time indices into their \(q+1\) residue classes.  Variables within each residue class are conditionally independent.  For centered independent variables \(Y_k\), expansion of the fourth power and (1) give
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\left(\sum_kY_k\right)^4\middle|M,\Omega\right]
 =\sum_k\mathbb E(Y_k^4\mid M,\Omega)
  +6\sum_{k<l}\mathbb E(Y_k^2\mid M,\Omega)
                    \mathbb E(Y_l^2\mid M,\Omega)
 \le C K^4\left(\sum_k a_k^2\right)^2
\]
when \(Y_k=a_k\epsilon_k\).  Combining the residue classes with
\( |x_0+\cdots+x_q|^4\le(q+1)^3\sum_{r=0}^q|x_r|^4 \) gives
\[
 \mathbb E(|Z_B|^4\mid M,\Omega)
 \le C_qK^4\left(\sum_{(j,u)\in B}\frac{w_{ju}^2}{s^2}\right)^2.
\tag{5}
\]
By Lyapunov's inequality, (5), the fact that every block contains at most \(k_n\) indices, and the definition of \(A_n,\delta_n\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_B\mathbb E(|Z_B|^3\mid M,\Omega)
 &\le C_qK^3
   \sum_B\left(\sum_{(j,u)\in B}\frac{w_{ju}^2}{s^2}\right)^{3/2}\\
 &\le C_qK^3
   \left(\max_B\sum_{(j,u)\in B}\frac{w_{ju}^2}{s^2}\right)^{1/2}A_n\\
 &\le C_qK^3\sqrt{k_n}\,\delta_n A_n=o(1).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]

It remains to identify the normalization.  Conditional row independence, conditional \(q\)-dependence, conditional centering, and \(\mathrm{ass:common\mbox{-}stationary\mbox{-}covariance}\) imply, directly from the displayed definition of \(s^2\),
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(L\mid M,\Omega)
 =\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{h=-q}^{q}\gamma(h)
    \sum_{u=1}^T w_{ju}w_{j,u+h}=s^2.
\tag{7}
\]
Here weights outside \(J\) are zero, as stipulated in \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}variance}\), and \(s>0\) follows from \(\mathrm{ass:frontier\mbox{-}variance\mbox{-}scale}\).  If
\[
 v_n^2:=\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_BZ_B\middle|M,\Omega\right),
\]
then \(L/s=\sum_BZ_B+R_n\), (4), (7), and conditional Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 |v_n^2-1|
 \le \operatorname{Var}(R_n\mid M,\Omega)
 +2\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(R_n\mid M,\Omega)}=o(1)
\tag{8}
\]
uniformly over the indicated laws and exponent triples.

For completeness, we now derive the independent-block normal approximation rather than invoke an external central limit theorem.  Put \(U_B=Z_B/v_n\), and let \(G_B\), conditionally independently over blocks, be centered Gaussian variables with \(\operatorname{Var}(G_B\mid M,\Omega)=\operatorname{Var}(U_B\mid M,\Omega)\).  Then \(\sum_BG_B\) is exactly standard normal.  For any three-times continuously differentiable \(f\) with bounded third derivative, replace the blocks one at a time and expand around the sum of all other terms.  The constant, linear, and quadratic terms cancel because \(U_B\) and \(G_B\) have the same first two moments; Taylor's remainder gives
\[
 \left|\mathbb Ef\!\left(\sum_BU_B\right)-\mathbb Ef\!\left(\sum_BG_B\right)\right|
 \le \frac{\|f'''\|_\infty}{6}
       \sum_B\{\mathbb E|U_B|^3+\mathbb E|G_B|^3\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Moreover, \(\mathbb E|G_B|^3=C\operatorname{Var}(U_B)^{3/2}\le C\mathbb E|U_B|^3\).  Equations (6) and (8) therefore make the right-hand side of (9) tend to zero uniformly.

Choose a fixed nonincreasing \(C^3\) cutoff \(\chi\) with \(\chi(x)=1\) for \(x\le0\) and \(\chi(x)=0\) for \(x\ge1\), and put \(f_{z,h}(x)=\chi((x-z)/h)\).  Its third derivative is bounded by \(C h^{-3}\), uniformly in \(z\).  Applying (9) to the upper and lower cutoff sandwiches gives, for each fixed \(h>0\),
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P\!\left(\sum_BU_B\le z\middle|M,\Omega\right)-\Phi(z)\right|
 \le \sup_z\{\Phi(z+h)-\Phi(z-h)\}+o(1)
 \le \frac{2h}{\sqrt{2\pi}}+o(1).
\]
First let \(n\to\infty\), and then let \(h\downarrow0\).  This proves the compact-uniform conditional normal approximation for \(\sum_BZ_B/v_n\).  By (8), rescaling by \(v_n\to1\) does not change the conclusion.  Finally, (4) and conditional Chebyshev imply \(R_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly.  The inequalities
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(\sum_BZ_B\le z-\varepsilon\middle|M,\Omega\right)
 -\mathbb P(|R_n|>\varepsilon\mid M,\Omega)
 \le \mathbb P(L/s\le z\mid M,\Omega)
\]
and the analogous upper bound with \(z+\varepsilon\), followed by \(n\to\infty\) and \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), establish
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P(L/s\le z\mid M,\Omega)-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0
\]
uniformly for \((a,b,c)\in\mathcal K\), as claimed.

proposed.name: Exponent-indexed signal--cohort--window class
proposed.construction: \(\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)=\{P_n:P_n\text{ governs }(M_n,\epsilon_n,Y_n(0),Y_n(1),A_n,G_n,S_n,W_n)\text{ and satisfies every member property listed for }\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)\text{ at index }n\}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The uniform conditional central limit claim requires conditional tail control. The existing conditional exponential-moment assumption must therefore be a member property of the exponent-indexed class.

proposed.statement: Conditional on \((M,\Omega)\), fixed \(q\), uniform sub-Gaussian moments, row-law factorization, conditional within-row block dependence, frontier variance nondegeneracy, and frontier score diffuseness imply \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|\mathbb P_P(L/s\le z\mid M,\Omega)-\Phi(z)|\to0\) uniformly when \((a,b,c)\) ranges over a compact subset of \([1/2,1]\times(0,1]\times[0,1]\).
proposed.justification: A blocking argument is uniform as the cohort and window exponents vary because the frontier weights are diffuse at their rescaled standard error.
proposed.gap: Available serial factor central limit theorems do not provide this compact-uniform exponent-indexed statement for deterministic causal-block masking.
proposed.consumer: The sharp-frontier achievability direction can focus on native-optimizer remainders rather than postulating a Gaussian leading score.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof conditions on the signal and hence uses the existing conditional exponential-moment node; the dependency list must record that fact.
